title: A REAL next to an integer or a decimal is compared and computed as a REAL; next to a DOUBLE as a DOUBLE; a DECIMAL casts to REAL correctly rounded
verdict: `real_col = 0.3` casts the constant to REAL (true for 0.3f); `real_col = 0.3::DOUBLE` widens the column (false); DECIMAL to REAL is the single nearest the exact decimal, halves to even
description: DuckDB brings a REAL (FLOAT) and an integer (any width) or a DECIMAL to a REAL, and a REAL and a DOUBLE to a DOUBLE: `typeof(0.3::REAL + 0.3)`, `typeof(0.3::REAL + 1)` and `typeof(0.3::REAL + 1::BIGINT)` are FLOAT; `typeof(0.3::REAL + 0.3::DOUBLE)` and `typeof(0.3::REAL + 1e0)` are DOUBLE. A comparison follows the same rule: `0.3::REAL = 0.3` is true (the decimal 0.3 is cast to the REAL 0.3f), `0.3::REAL = 0.3::DOUBLE` is false, `16777216::REAL = 16777217` and `16777216::REAL = 16777217::BIGINT` are true (the integer rounds to the REAL 16777216). A plain decimal literal is a DECIMAL (`typeof(0.3)` is DECIMAL(2,1), `typeof(1.0000000000000000000001)` DECIMAL(23,22)); a literal with an exponent (`1e0`) or past 38 digits is a DOUBLE.

The cast of a DECIMAL to REAL gives the single nearest the exact decimal, halves to even, in every probed case: 59,100 decimals of precision 7 to 38 and scale 0 to 38, among them 33,000 within one unit of the last place of a midpoint between two adjacent singles at scales 10, 12, 15, 20, 31, 35 and 38. Going through a double first (decimal to double to single) would round twice; DuckDB does not.
An integer casts to REAL with one rounding: `CAST(16777217::INTEGER AS REAL)` is 16777216, `CAST(9007199254740993::BIGINT AS REAL)` is 9007199254740992.
reference: The SQL lift brings a REAL and an integer or decimal to REAL and a REAL and a DOUBLE to DOUBLE (`_Lift.common`, #1908, ruling 186 P1). Only a constant is brought to REAL: the frontend folds it to an `fp32` literal (`castConst`) and refuses a cast of a column to REAL (P2). The fold rounds once, as DuckDB: an integer only within 2^53 (exactly a double), a decimal or string only where its nearest double is not a midpoint between two singles, so that the double's rounding to a single is the decimal's (P3); outside those it refuses.

provenance.checked_by: types-casts session (duckdb 2.0.0, Python 3.12, macOS arm64), for #1908 / ruling 186

evidence.sql: SELECT typeof(0.3::REAL + 0.3), typeof(0.3::REAL + 1), typeof(0.3::REAL + 1::BIGINT), typeof(0.3::REAL + 0.3::DOUBLE), typeof(0.3::REAL + 1e0)
SELECT CAST(16777217::INTEGER AS REAL), CAST(9007199254740993::BIGINT AS REAL)
SELECT CAST(CAST('<m / 10^s>' AS DECIMAL(p, s)) AS REAL) for 42,600 decimals, compared bit for bit with the single nearest m / 10^s computed exactly (Python Fraction, halves to even)
evidence.observed: 0 mismatches; precision 7 to 38, scale 0 to 30, 24,000 of them within one unit of a midpoint between adjacent singles

provenance.notes: The decimal probe draws 300 random unscaled values for each (precision, scale) in {7, 9, 12, 15, 18, 20, 25, 30, 38} x {0, 1, 3, 6, 10, 11, 15, 20, 30} with scale <= precision (seed 1), and for 2,000 random adjacent singles below 1e6 in magnitude the decimals floor(mid * 10^s) + {-1, 0, 1} at s in {10, 12, 15, 20}.
